caption_hazard: The first lecture uses paper, color, cutting, and side language, so captions can make it sound like a craft step. The mathematical claim is about a finished strip whose full walk changes the side information a local patch seemed to keep stable.
safe_claim: The supported claim is that the Mobius strip makes the course method visible: build the object by a gluing rule, follow a mark all the way around it, and notice that the completed surface can defeat what every small flat neighborhood seemed to promise.
repair_move: If a sentence says only that the strip has one side, add the walk-around test. Carry a mark or traveler around once, record how it returns, and connect that result to the gluing rule rather than to the paper's thickness or neatness.
do_not_claim: Do not claim that all later topology ignores measurement or physical shape. The first lecture separates side behavior from exact shape so the reader can see what survives stretching, but geometry still matters whenever the question asks for length, angle, area, or smoothness.
reviewer_question: Evidence check: name the traveler or mark, follow one full trip, state what side information returns changed, and explain why no small flat patch could expose that whole-surface behavior before the strip is completed.

caption_hazard: Disk routing language can sound like a drawing puzzle where the problem is crowded ink. Captions may keep words such as curve and intersect while hiding the deeper point: the obstruction concerns every legal drawing with the same endpoint order.
safe_claim: The supported claim is that the lecture turns a routing puzzle into a rule-governed deformation problem. The endpoints, their circular order, and the no-crossing rule decide whether any allowed redrawing must inherit the same obstruction.
repair_move: When a paragraph says a connection is impossible, add the protected feature that defeats every legal attempt. Name the boundary order, the allowed motion of paths, and the reason the crossing cannot be removed by choosing a cleaner sketch.
do_not_claim: Do not treat one crowded drawing as the proof or blame the impossibility on poor layout. The proof needs a reason that survives any allowed redrawing while endpoints, endpoint order, and no-crossing rules stay fixed.
reviewer_question: Evidence check: name the boundary data before the drawing, state how paths may move, and show why the forbidden crossing is forced by the setup itself rather than by one crowded or unlucky sketch.

caption_hazard: Words such as product, quotient, surgery, and manifold can be misheard as labels for finished objects. The source risk is losing the making rule, which is where the mathematical meaning sits before any short formal name is useful.
safe_claim: The supported claim is that the lecture teaches space-making as a mathematical act. Independent choices make products, declared sameness makes quotients, local patches make manifolds, and controlled replacement makes surgery meaningful because each operation changes which routes and neighborhoods exist.
repair_move: If a sentence names a space, add how it was made. Say which choices are independent, which pieces are paired or glued, what was removed or thickened, and what a traveler is allowed to do afterward.
do_not_claim: Do not let product, quotient, manifold, or surgery appear as unexplained vocabulary pasted onto the paragraph. The independent choices, imposed identifications, local test, or replacement boundary must be visible before the formal word is allowed to shorten the sentence.
reviewer_question: Evidence check: reconstruct the space from the rule alone by naming the choices, identifications, local patches, or replacement boundary before using product, quotient, manifold, or surgery as a shortcut for the completed construction.

caption_hazard: Gluing and boundary words can make the drawn square look like the object itself. Captions may not signal that arrows and labels are instructions for building a surface, so the reader may reason from the wrong object.
safe_claim: The supported claim is that edge identifications are instructions for the finished surface. They decide where a traveler re-enters, whether an apparent border remains a border, and whether a local direction choice survives a full loop.
repair_move: When a page reasons from a square, add a sentence that applies the gluing rule before drawing conclusions. The repair should say what points become identical and how paths, boundary, orientation, or apparent edges behave after the identification.
do_not_claim: Do not call the unglued drawing the final surface or treat its outside edges as physical borders by default. It is a code for a surface that exists only after the stated identifications are actually made.
reviewer_question: Evidence check: say which points become identical, how a path crosses the glued edge afterward, and which boundary or orientation claim would be false if the flat square were read literally instead of as instructions.

caption_hazard: Classification, orientable, handle, and boundary can sound like a naming exercise. The course point is not to memorize surface labels, but to see which features remain after cutting, gluing, stretching, and redrawing have removed accidental appearances.
safe_claim: The supported claim is that surface classification is about durable evidence after legal rearrangement. Handles preserve route choices, boundary pieces preserve edge behavior, and orientability records whether side choices can agree globally across the whole surface.
repair_move: If a paragraph lists surface types, add the test that tells them apart. Ask what happens to loops, sides, handles, or boundary under legal changes, and explain why those checks survive a different drawing of the same surface.
do_not_claim: Do not imply every visual difference creates a new surface type or that a surface name by itself explains the case. Classification earns its force because many drawings represent the same underlying surface once the surviving features have been checked.
reviewer_question: Evidence check: name the surviving feature after the cuts and gluings, explain how a different drawing would still carry it, and do not treat a surface name as the proof that the classification has been earned.

caption_hazard: Dimension and submanifold language can sound abstract before the physical question is clear. The lecture asks an everyday room question first: when two moving things have enough freedom, can a small legal nudge separate accidental meetings from unavoidable ones?
safe_claim: The supported claim is that the lecture uses dimension and ordinary position to separate accidental contact from evidence. After a legal nudge, some meetings disappear, while clean remaining meetings can be counted, signed, or inspected without depending on a messy drawing.
repair_move: When a sentence mentions generic position, add the ordinary picture it creates. The repair should describe clean meetings, separated events, and counts or signs that can be assigned after the legal nudge without changing the original placement question.
do_not_claim: Do not treat every visible meeting as forced or every disappearance as meaningless. The page must distinguish a removable accident from a meeting protected by the setup after the objects have been placed in ordinary position.
reviewer_question: Evidence check: identify the accident removed by the small nudge, the meeting pattern that remains, and the reason the nudge preserves the original placement question instead of quietly replacing it with a different problem.

caption_hazard: Center-of-gravity language can pull the reader toward physics alone. The mathematical point is the forced passage through a special state under continuous change, where a watched quantity cannot jump across the required balance condition.
safe_claim: The supported claim is that the balance demonstration gives a first existence argument. A continuously changing quantity cannot pass from one side of the required condition to the other without meeting it somewhere, even if the lecture does not compute where.
repair_move: If a paragraph stays with balance intuition, add the quantity being watched, the two sides of the comparison, and the special equality that no-jump motion forces. Then state that the argument proves existence, not a recipe for finding the place.
do_not_claim: Do not say the physical demonstration proves every later theorem or replaces their assumptions. It supplies the shared pattern of continuous motion, comparison, and forced meeting; each later theorem still needs its own object, domain, and rule.
reviewer_question: Evidence check: identify the changing quantity, the condition it cannot skip, and the exact claim limit. The repaired claim proves the existence of a special state rather than claiming a computation of its location.

caption_hazard: Positive and negative intersection words can be copied as signs without explaining where signs come from. The source risk is arithmetic without orientation, where plus and minus look like loose labels instead of evidence tied to local direction.
safe_claim: The supported claim is that the lecture repairs raw crossing counts by giving clean meetings signs. Pair events created or removed during legal motion then contribute no net change, so the signed total becomes the quantity worth protecting.
repair_move: When a page uses plus and minus intersections, add the shared orientation or local direction rule. Then show one birth or death event where the two signs cancel, so the arithmetic is tied to a visible motion.
do_not_claim: Do not call the raw number of crossings invariant or let sign language stand alone. The protected candidate is the signed total after the page has explained clean meetings, orientation, and why pair cancellation is allowed.
reviewer_question: Evidence check: show where the signs come from, why a newly born pair contributes opposite signs, and what legal motion leaves the signed total unchanged while allowing the raw number of crossings to change.

caption_hazard: This lecture has a missing-caption middle part, so any claim about the full transition from maps to fixed points needs extra caution. The available source supports the surrounding arc, not every hidden sentence or intermediate explanation.
safe_claim: The supported claim is the graph-diagonal translation. A rule becomes its graph, the diagonal records self-agreement, and a meeting between them is a fixed point, while the missing-caption gap limits stronger claims about the lecture's exact route.
repair_move: If a sentence depends on the absent middle caption, weaken it to the recovered structure. Stay with map, graph, diagonal, self-agreement, and controlled intersection language, and mark any bridge beyond that as course-arc inference.
do_not_claim: Do not present the missing section as transcript-verified or quote it as if the words were available. Mark it as course-arc inference unless a human check of the video supplies stronger evidence for the exact transition.
reviewer_question: Evidence check: justify the claim from recovered captions and visible lecture structure, and keep it at graph, diagonal, and self-agreement unless a human check supplies the missing middle evidence needed for a stronger statement.

caption_hazard: Brouwer, closed ball, boundary, and continuous can make the theorem sound like a slogan. The reader needs the filled space, the rule that sends it back into itself, and the no-jump condition before the name carries meaning.
safe_claim: The supported claim is Brouwer's fixed-point contract in plain terms. A continuous rule from a closed filled ball back into itself cannot move every point away from itself; at least one point must be sent to itself.
repair_move: When Brouwer is named, add the four checks: closed filled ball, map back into itself, continuity, and fixed-point conclusion. Also say what the theorem does not supply: a location, uniqueness, or solved motion path.
do_not_claim: Do not use Brouwer as a general statement that every motion has a fixed point or that every process returns somewhere. The object, self-map rule, closedness, and continuity condition are part of the theorem's force.
reviewer_question: Evidence check: name the closed filled space, the self-map rule, the no-jump condition, and the conclusion limit. The claim is at least one fixed point, not its location, uniqueness, or an algorithm for finding it.

caption_hazard: Vector field, equilibrium, differential equation, and index can collapse into one motion vocabulary. The lecture separates the arrows, the vanishing points, and what can be learned from nearby turning before any path is solved.
safe_claim: The supported claim is that vector fields let the course study motion by reading an arrow pattern. Where arrows vanish, how nearby arrows turn, and what the local pattern forces can be studied before trajectories are solved.
repair_move: If a paragraph says the system has an equilibrium, add how the arrow field behaves nearby and what question remains after the point is found. The repair should distinguish locating a zero from understanding the local turn pattern.
do_not_claim: Do not treat an equilibrium as the same object as a fixed point of a map unless the map or motion law has been named. A vanishing arrow, a return point, and a solved trajectory are related but not interchangeable.
reviewer_question: Evidence check: point to the field, isolate the vanishing point, walk around it in nearby arrows, and keep that local evidence separate from a fixed point of an unnamed map or a solution path not yet computed.

caption_hazard: Index and Euler characteristic can sound like two names for one number. The lecture is about two levels of evidence: local arrow turning near each defect and the whole-surface account those local entries must eventually match.
safe_claim: The supported claim is that isolated vector-field defects carry local signed evidence. Only the total over all defects on the same surface, under the needed boundary or cleanup assumptions, is ready to be compared with the surface account.
repair_move: When a page adds indices, add the scope of the sum. Every isolated defect on the same surface must be included, and the boundary condition, cleanup step, or reason no defect is missing must be named.
do_not_claim: Do not compare one local index directly with Euler characteristic as if it were the whole theorem. The comparison belongs to the completed same-surface ledger after all local defects have been counted under the right assumptions.
reviewer_question: Evidence check: distinguish one defect's local turning from the complete same-surface index sum, then name the surface number that total is allowed to meet and the condition that makes the comparison legal.

caption_hazard: Poincare-Hopf and hairy-ball language can become a memorable phrase without the bookkeeping contract. The theorem needs a chosen surface, a vector field on it, isolated defects, local index assignments, and a complete total.
safe_claim: The supported claim is the Poincare-Hopf ledger. After all isolated defects of a vector field on the same surface are counted with local index, their total is tied to that surface's Euler characteristic.
repair_move: If a sentence says topology predicts motion, add the mechanism. List the defects, assign local indices, add them over the same surface, and compare that complete total with the surface invariant rather than speaking in broad prediction language.
do_not_claim: Do not say the theorem solves the differential equation or gives exact motion paths. It constrains possible defects and equilibria before exact solutions are known, and only after the theorem's surface and defect conditions are in place.
reviewer_question: Evidence check: name the surface, list the complete defect account, state how local indices are assigned, and say what stronger motion claim the theorem does not provide beyond the total constraint.

caption_hazard: Applications, rotation, state space, and dynamical-system language can make examples look unrelated. The source risk is missing the shared idea: replace the physical story with a space of possible states, then study the shape and forbidden regions of that space.
safe_claim: The supported claim is that applications reuse the earlier method only after translation. Build the state space, remove forbidden states, interpret paths as legal motions, and read the topological constraint inside that model.
repair_move: When an application appears, add the model behind it. Say what one point of the state space represents, what movement inside that space means, which states are forbidden, and which earlier course constraint is being reused.
do_not_claim: Do not treat a physical example as automatically solved by topology or skip the modeling step. The topological claim only applies after the model matches the allowed states, forbidden states, freedoms, and boundary conditions.
reviewer_question: Evidence check: say what one state records, which physical impossibilities were removed, how a path in the model becomes a real motion, and which claim would overreach the model because the translation was not justified.

caption_hazard: The final pictorial-thinking summary can sound like an aesthetic preference. The course is not saying pictures are nice; it is saying pictures can carry rules, allowed moves, forbidden moves, protected evidence, and claim limits.
safe_claim: The supported claim is that the final lecture gathers a reusable proof habit. Make the object visible, state the allowed and forbidden moves, protect the evidence, then draw only the conclusion that the evidence can carry.
repair_move: If a conclusion says pictorial thinking matters, add the proof contract a picture must satisfy. Name the object, allowed move, forbidden move, protected fact, failure test, and the exact claim boundary before praising the picture.
do_not_claim: Do not reduce the course to visual intuition or say the pictures replace proof. The pictures expose constraints that can be audited: route order, gluing rules, signed counts, fixed-point meetings, defect totals, and model limits.
reviewer_question: Evidence check: use the final summary on an earlier lecture by naming its object, legal move, protected fact, failure condition, and claim boundary, then state what the picture alone would not prove.
